assets.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: finished short-story book cover, portrait 9:16, exactly 864 by 1536 pixels. Create a new composition for "The Return Tray", a dry comic story about a regularly resurrecting adult magical girl and the mortuary attendant she plays chess with. The attached orchard painting is a BRUSHWORK AND COLOUR-MASS reference only; do not reproduce its orchard or landscape.
Canadian Group of Seven inspired oil painting, broad rhythmic colour/value shapes, directional opaque strokes, selective impasto, connected shadows and lost edges. Quiet, human, wry. Not glossy anime, not horror, no gore.
A clean mortuary interior: high frosted window, steel slab, a low overhead light fitting, modest desk with a worn closed folding chess set, digital chess clock and small steel effects tray. Central figure: Leonie / Princess Snapdragon, explicitly a twenty-nine-year-old woman, dark chin-length bob, practical adult face. Sitting on the slab fully alive, yawning with one hand near her mouth and a slightly irritated expression, looking towards the foreground desk. Fully clothed heroic jacket in muted rose/cream with ONE enormous rose at a shoulder, small cuff flowers, gloves with grey-stained fingertips, sober dark trousers. ONE bright yellow boot on her anatomical right foot; anatomical left boot missing, black sock with a small heel hole. ONE dangling silver chandelier-like earring in her right ear, left one absent. Coherent anatomy, ordinary human body, no wounds. The missing boot is a comic practical nuisance.
Compose as an inviting novel cover, not a montage or plot summary: her tired posture and the small chess clock form the visual question; connected muted green/cream shadows, rose and yellow as economical accents, motivated afternoon window light. The attendant's identity need not be shown.
Exact title rendered ONCE, large legible painterly serif type within generous safe margins in the upper quarter: "The Return Tray". No author credit, no other text, no border or watermark. Keep all title and subject elements safe for 9:16.
